verdicts.evidence: On the authors' bundled sim.rda (6000 rows, 1965 events, 6 batches), COLSA's sequential estimates match pooled coxph coefficients to within 0.0021 and SE ratios fall in [0.983, 1.021]; model object memory stays flat at ~10 KB across all six updates (max/min ratio 1.06), concretely demonstrating equal efficiency and constant memory.

Over the full Figure-2 grid K∈{6,20,50,200} with the paper's Appendix-B DGP, COLSA matches Oracle RMSE within 0.001 at every K, beats streaming SGD and Meta at every K (e.g., K200: 0.0245 vs 0.1316 and 0.0445), and is the only online method holding nominal coverage at K200 (0.960 vs Meta 0.793, Online 0.840); the Online baseline is disclosed as a conservative upper bound (pchreg on cumulative data, not the true streaming Wu-2021 scheme), and at small K it edges COLSA on RMSE by ~0.003.

overall: The logbook provides concrete experimental evidence at the paper's own scale supporting both claims: Claim 1 via coefficient/SE agreement and flat memory on the bundled dataset, Claim 2 via a full-grid simulation showing COLSA matching Oracle and beating genuine streaming competitors. Key limitations—single dataset for Claim 1, an upper-bound rather than faithful Online baseline, and reduced replications at large K—are transparently disclosed but do not overturn the supporting evidence.
